method: A single anonymised hand-off of 176 PNGs whose names are 16 hex characters. The feature audit was made afterwards, with the contract open, against the same renders.
supersedes: 5.0.0, in full. 5.0.0 covered 10 of the subjects the contract renders and left 44 NEVER CHECKED, and by this run three of its verdicts - officer, dufferin-terrace-toboggan-run and halifax-quayside - had gone STALE because the art moved under them. This record replaces it because it covers all 54 subjects that have a render, and because a partial record that reads like a full one is the failure this file exists to refuse.

scope.unrenderedIsNotAVerdict: Neither subject was handed over and neither is audited here. Both are UNRENDERED BY DECISION: their renders would be repeating, droppable parallax tiles that the art bible forbids putting an identifying feature on, so a verifier able to name Ottawa or Quebec City from them would be reporting a defect. An audit of an image nobody was shown would be the quietest kind of false pass, and the scorer fails one on purpose.
scope.countsAreDerived: Every number in this block is what scripts/lib/art-score.mjs reports for this record over the tree it is committed into, not a number anyone typed. `make verify-art` prints the same ones.

runIntegrity.blindnessCaveat: partial - see primingLeak. One leak is declared: the environment printed recent commit subjects naming a bicycle, Toronto and foothills before any render was opened. No identification in this run is marked primed, and the two subjects the leak could have touched were answered without naming the place.
whatIsProven: The 176 identifications in handoffRun.answers were written from image bytes alone, under opaque 16-hex names, with no filename, label, contract or reference photograph in view.

They were hashed by verify-art commit BEFORE verify-art reveal opened the keymap, and score re-checked the hash against the file on disk. It matched. The blind pass was not revised with the answer key open.

Every source digest in the keymap was re-derived against the tree THIS RUN WAS MADE FROM and every one matched. That is no longer true of the tree this record now lives in: two subjects were redrawn on main before this record was carried across, and their verdicts are withdrawn rather than restated. For the other 52 subjects the digests still match, so those verdicts are about the art on disk today.
whatIsNotProven: That the identifier read nothing outside the hand-off directory. Only the hand-off can give that, and this record cannot recover it after the fact. What it can say is stated in primingLeak.

That the small rungs of the size ladder measure recognition. They do not, and cannot in this hand-off shape: the same identifier saw the full-size render of every subject first, so a w140 answer measures retention of what was already recognised, not recognition at w140.
runIntegrity.whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Scoring proves a stated verdict matches the contract. It cannot prove the verdict was made blind; only the hand-off gives that, and only if the identifier did not go and look. The one thing visible before the answers were fixed is declared in primingLeak.

artMovedSince.what: Two subjects whose art was redrawn between the branch this run was made on and the tree this record now lives in. Their verdicts assert nothing about today's drawings.
artMovedSince.howItIsEnforced: Not by this prose. Every keymap entry carries the sha256 of the SVG bytes it was drawn from and the scorer re-derives them on every run, so these two report as STALE ART and `make verify-art` exits 1 until a fresh blind run covers them. A record cannot go quietly green while the art moves under it.
artMovedSince.whatWouldClearIt: A new hand-off and a new blind verdict for both, by a verifier that did not write this record. Nothing else: not time, not a re-read of the old words, and not the opinion of whoever redrew them.

findings.maskProbesHeld: Twelve renders were mask probes with a required feature painted out. In every one the blind answer reported the feature as ABSENT and never claimed a masked feature was present: the five-sails National Flag, the beaver paddle tail twice, the beaver incisors twice, the officer felt hat twice, the officer striped breeches twice, the Peace Tower flag, the Chateau Frontenac central tower and the CN Tower observation pod. The two renders that looked like a broken rig (a torso with floating boots) and a snapped-off tower were these probes, not art defects.
findings.twoKindsOfIdentificationFailure: Of 24 failing subjects, 14 failed only because the unprompted answer lacked an accepted phrase while describing the right thing - pump-jack was answered An oil pumpjack on a wellsite against an expected a pumpjack; streetcar was answered A modern low-floor articulated streetcar against an expected a streetcar. Those are matcher or contract artefacts. Six are genuine art misses: granite-erratic, driftwood-pile, city-wall, dufferin-terrace-toboggan-run, pier-21 and marina-boats. RESOLVED, 2026-09-17, for nine of the fourteen: the comparator was the defect and it was fixed rather than the contracts widened. log-rail-gate, pump-jack, player, player-on-a-toboggan, streetcar, player-on-skates, toronto-trail, player-on-a-skateboard and city-wall had all named their subject. Six subjects are still unidentified and five of them are genuine art misses: dufferin-terrace-toboggan-run, pier-21, marina-boats, driftwood-pile and granite-erratic, whose art has since been redrawn and which is no longer judged here. The sixth, ranch-barn, is a vocabulary question and not an art one - the verdict says paddock where the contract says corral - and the comparator deliberately does not guess synonyms, because a table of them in the scorer would be a dictionary of answers that nobody owns. It is on the contract owner's list below.
findings.legibilityAtHandedOverSizes: Several background strips lose their subject at the sizes handed over. alberta-foothills-rangeland is the clearest: the grazing cattle that are the point of the strip are invisible at w140 and three red specks at w300. peggys-cove-barrens, halifax-quayside and winnipeg-riverwalk lose their boats and figures the same way.
findings.artRuleAgainstTheWorkingAgreement: Outline on characters only HOLDS - player, officer and guide carry outlines and no landmark or prop does. Three-tone cel shading HOLDS. Bold rounded shapes HOLD everywhere except the ranch-barn horse, which is faceted and off-model. Saturated palette DOES NOT HOLD on granite-erratic, driftwood-pile and grain-bins, drawn in flat near-neutral greys, and that desaturation is why two of them could not be identified at any size. Reference-accurate and simplified, never invented HOLDS for the named landmarks: peace-tower, cn-tower, nathan-phillips-square, chateau-frontenac, peggys-cove-light, library-of-parliament, town-clock, five-sails and human-rights-museum each passed feature by feature.

recommendationsToTheContractOwner: DONE, and it was the matcher rather than the contracts. The first recommendation here asked for expectedBlindAnswer to be widened or the insertion allowance raised. Neither was done: scripts/lib/art-score.mjs now compares CONTENT WORDS rather than phrases, so an article, an adjective, a different word order and a wider gap all stop being wrong answers, and no contract had to be loosened to make an honest verdict pass. Nine subjects were affected.

STILL OPEN, and it is yours rather than the matcher's: ranch-barn. The verdict says "paddock" where the contract accepts "corral". Both are correct words for the same enclosure, and the matcher refuses to guess that - a synonym table in the scorer would be a dictionary of answers, unbounded and reviewed by nobody. Either accept the second word in expectedBlindAnswer or leave it and accept that a verifier using it will be marked wrong.

STILL OPEN: player-on-a-bicycle's `neverAdd` on a helmet. It is not being breached - there is no helmet in the art - and the subject still fails, because the toque reads as one. A prohibition cannot answer this. See the routed finding.
The identifier answered all four ride subjects correctly in substance and each still failed; that pattern across a whole family points at the contract, not at the rig.
Consider whether alberta-foothills-rangeland should be judged at w140 at all: the cattle it requires cannot be seen there, so the size ladder asks a question the art cannot answer.
howToReadAFailInThisRecord: A fail is one of three things and they need different fixes: the unprompted answer did not contain an accepted phrase (usually a contract or matcher problem - see recommendationsToTheContractOwner), a mustBeRight feature was audited ABSENT (an art problem), or a neverAdd feature was found PRESENT (an art problem). The per-subject row says which, and featuresMissing and forbiddenPresent name it exactly.
amendedBy: infra. NOT a second verification pass: no render was opened, no picture was judged and no answer was edited. `handoffRun` - keymap, answers and audit - is byte-for-byte the run the art-verifier committed.

identifications.cues: Red-and-black funnel; stacked wheelhouse over deckhouse; heavy round fenders the full length of the hull; stubby high-freeboard workboat proportions; brown wooden rubbing strake at the waterline
identifications.moreCertain: A towing winch or hawser would confirm tug over fishing boat; a name or port on the bow would place it

identifications.answer: Two cartoon characters standing side by side facing each other: on the left a woman with long dark hair in a blue winter parka, red scarf, red mittens, grey trousers with white cuffs and brown boots; on the right an upright anthropomorphic beaver - brown fur, cream belly and muzzle, two large orange-white incisors, small round ear, and a broad flat cross-hatched paddle tail resting behind. Both are outlined; the beaver is unmistakably a beaver.
identifications.cues: Beaver: paired buck incisors, scaly flat paddle tail, small rounded ear, stocky upright body. Woman: winter parka and scarf, mittens, boots - dressed for cold
identifications.moreCertain: The beaver is clear. For the woman, any role marker - a uniform, a tool, a badge - would say who she is meant to be rather than just what she is wearing. Her arms also hang almost straight with little shoulder articulation

identifications.answer: A small fishing settlement on bare rock: a line of red, white and grey gable-roofed sheds or stages raised on a timber boardwalk over a channel of water, three small boats moored alongside, a dense spruce treeline behind, and a broad sheet of glacier-scoured grey bedrock in the foreground with meltwater pools and patches of moss. Reads as an outport or Shield-country fishing village; I cannot name it.
identifications.cues: Fishing stages on pilings with a continuous plank walkway; small open boats; sawtooth spruce horizon; foreground bedrock drawn with sweeping striation lines and standing pools - glaciated rock, not soil
identifications.moreCertain: A headland, a lighthouse, a church, or the shape of the harbour mouth. The building type says Atlantic outport but the bare striated rock could equally be the Shield

identifications.answer: An upright cartoon beaver standing on two feet in a three-quarter view: brown fur with a cream belly panel and muzzle, two big orange-white front teeth, a small round ear, dark eyes, short arms and a broad flat cross-hatched paddle tail trailing behind. Clearly a beaver.
identifications.cues: Paired buck incisors; flat scaly paddle tail with a cross-hatch texture; small rounded ear set high; stocky barrel body with cream belly; short clawed feet
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to identify the animal. To judge the pose I would want a clearer read on the far arm, which merges into the body outline here

identifications.answer: An urban waterfront park promenade: a terraced stone and brick embankment, a paved walkway with globe lampposts and wooden benches, three broad round-crowned trees (two in autumn brown, one green), a scatter of small standing figures, a pale blue strip of water behind, and a flat grey skyline of generic office towers on the far shore. A city park layer - the skyline names no city.
identifications.cues: Banded masonry retaining wall in courses; street furniture repeated at intervals; lollipop trees with a single highlight blob; distant towers drawn as plain rectangles with window rows and no distinguishing silhouette
identifications.moreCertain: One identifiable building in the skyline. As drawn every tower is a grey box, so this could be any waterfront in the country

identifications.answer: A row of four farm grain storage bins on a concrete pad: tall tan-grey cylinders with conical peaked roofs and small roof caps, a ladder climbing the second one, and dark hopper cones underneath standing on legs. Hopper-bottom grain bins - prairie farm storage. Not a wooden grain elevator.
identifications.cues: Conical roof caps with a central vent; hopper cones on steel legs, which is bin rather than elevator construction; access ladder; identical units in a row on a poured pad
identifications.moreCertain: Scale against a truck or a person, and a farmyard around it. Also worth noting: if a wooden prairie grain elevator was intended, this is not one - there is no tall square headhouse or driveway shed

identifications.answer: Three Hereford cattle standing on grass in profile facing right - a full-grown cow with two progressively smaller calves behind her. Red-brown bodies with the breed's distinctive white face, white throat and white lower legs.
identifications.cues: Red body with a clean white face and white stockings - the Hereford marking pattern; blocky beef conformation with a straight topline; three sizes stepping back, reading as a cow with calves; short grass strip underfoot
identifications.moreCertain: Horn or poll detail and a clearer ear and muzzle at this size; the heads are small enough that the white face is doing all the breed identification

identifications.answer: A canal lock seen head-on: a pair of mitre gates closed against each other in a shallow V, set between dressed stone chamber walls, with dark railed catwalks along the tops of both walls and water in front of and behind the gates. A working lock chamber - no name attaches.
identifications.cues: Two leaves meeting at a centre post to form a mitre pointing upstream - the defining shape of a lock gate; coursed ashlar block walls either side; horizontal strapping bands across the gate leaves; walkway railings above
identifications.moreCertain: The balance beams that swing the gates, a lock-keeper's hut, or a boat in the chamber. The gates are drawn closed and flat-on, which hides most of the mechanism

identifications.answer: Toronto City Hall - Viljo Revell's New City Hall on Nathan Phillips Square. Two curved concave slab towers of unequal height standing back to back, cradling the low saucer-shaped council chamber between them, all sitting on a long podium with a colonnade and a blue reflecting pool across the front. A named landmark and I am confident.
identifications.cues: The paired curved towers of different heights facing each other - a silhouette nothing else shares; the domed clamshell council chamber nested between their inner faces; banded window strips on the concave elevations; podium colonnade with the rectangular reflecting pool in front
identifications.moreCertain: The Freedom Arches or the square's crowd would confirm the setting, but the building alone is decisive

identifications.answer: Canada Place, Vancouver - the sail-roofed cruise terminal and convention centre on Burrard Inlet, here shown smaller and with a Canadian flag flying from the centre of the roof. Same building as another image in this set; the maple-leaf flag settles the country.
identifications.cues: Five white fabric sail peaks with masts and stay lines; long white pier block with two window bands beneath; Canadian flag at the centre of the sail line; dark pier deck over water
identifications.moreCertain: The North Shore mountains or the downtown towers behind it - the building is shown in isolation, so the city is inferred from the roof alone

identifications.answer: A saddled bay riding horse standing in profile facing right, drawn large: reddish-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs, a tan leather saddle with a girth and a hanging stirrup, and a bridle with a browband, cheekpiece, bit and reins running forward. Anatomically sound and on-model - rounded forms, clean three-tone shading, no outline. No rider and no unit markings.
identifications.cues: Bay colour with black points; correct equine proportions - withers, croup, hock and stifle all where they belong; tack drawn as separate saddle, girth, stirrup leather and bridle; weight settled on all four feet with a soft cast shadow
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to call it a horse. To call it a particular working horse - police mount, ranch horse, draught - I would need the saddle blanket, brand or harness that says so

identifications.answer: A farmers' market produce stall: a wooden trestle table under a green-and-white scalloped striped awning on two posts, with crates of produce on the counter - red fruit or tomatoes, pale loaves or roots, and green vegetables - a sack leaning at the left, a crate or sign board below the table and a broom or bundle at the right.
identifications.cues: Scalloped market awning in green and white stripes; open-fronted trestle counter; produce shown as grouped coloured blobs in wooden crates; hessian sack on the ground
identifications.moreCertain: Legible goods or a price board. The produce is generic coloured lumps at this size, so it says market rather than which market or what is being sold

identifications.answer: I cannot tell. Enlarged, it is a low flat object in undifferentiated grey-beige: two long horizontal bars or rails with dark discs at their ends, a shorter pale platform below them, a small cluster of three or four short prongs standing up near the left, and a dark ground strip underneath. There is no colour anywhere and no detail that resolves. My best guesses would be a sled or sledge with upright handles, a cart, or a piece of low machinery, but I would not stand behind any of them.
identifications.cues: Long paired horizontal members reading as runners or shafts; dark circular ends that could be wheel hubs or pole caps; a small upright pronged cluster; everything in two or three near-identical greys, so form is carried only by silhouette
identifications.moreCertain: Colour, or any surface marking at all. This render may be a deliberately desaturated or painted-over probe rather than the finished asset - I cannot tell which from inside the hand-off, and that distinction is exactly what I would need

identifications.answer: A canal lock with its mitre gates closed, shown small: two gate leaves meeting at a centre post between coursed stone chamber walls, dark railings on the walls above, pale water below. Same lock as another image in this set, at a smaller size.
identifications.cues: V-shaped pair of gate leaves meeting mid-channel; ashlar stonework either side; railed walkways on the copings; horizontal bands across the gates
identifications.moreCertain: At this size the gate strapping and the railings are almost the only detail left; balance beams or a boat in the chamber would carry the reading down to small sizes better

identifications.answer: A heritage streetcar on a town street, drawn large: a green-and-cream tram with a clerestory roof and a row of windows standing on rails, a pale terminal or works building behind it with twin chimneys and a red-and-white awning, a three-storey red-brick block with an arched entrance and a canopy at the centre, and a plain white building to the right. Same scene as a smaller image in this set. A generic early-1900s streetcar street, not a place I can name.
identifications.cues: Clerestory-roofed tram in green with a yellow waist stripe and spoked trucks; street rails running the width of the image; brick commercial block with segmental-arched windows and a corbel cornice; industrial chimneys behind
identifications.moreCertain: A route number, a destination board or a company name on the tram, or a civic landmark behind it. The tram is the most specific thing here and it carries no lettering

identifications.answer: A coastal waterfront promenade: a grey paved walkway and green verge behind a white picket rail, wooden benches and twin-globe lampposts, four people standing looking out, two tall spruce, and a deep blue sea carrying a white passenger ferry and a dark red freighter, with gulls above and a forested far shore under a grey industrial or city skyline. A working seaport park - I cannot name the port.
identifications.cues: White ferry with a squat funnel and a red boot stripe; long low dark-red bulk carrier; picket rail and benches facing the water; spruce on the verge; distant shoreline of conifers with grey towers and stacks behind
identifications.moreCertain: A named vessel, a terminal building, or a recognisable headland or bridge. The ferry plus freighter says a real harbour but the skyline is anonymous blocks

identifications.answer: The same rock-shore fishing settlement as another image in this set, shown much smaller: red and white sheds on a boardwalk over water, small boats, a spruce treeline, and a wide foreground of scoured grey bedrock with pools. At this size the boats and the walkway have almost dissolved and the image reads mainly as grey rock with a coloured band across it.
identifications.cues: Row of coloured gable sheds reduced to blocks; sawtooth conifer horizon; dominant grey striated rock foreground; blue water pools
identifications.moreCertain: This is a legibility problem rather than an identification one: the buildings survive the size reduction but the boats, walkway and stages do not, so what the place is for stops being readable

identifications.answer: A ranch or pasture background strip: rolling green hills behind, a long post-and-rail fence running the width, rough grazing with scattered bushes, a bare dirt track along the bottom, and three red-brown cattle with white faces - Herefords - grazing along the fence line. Drawn very small; I had to enlarge it to see the cattle at all.
identifications.cues: Continuous rail fence with regularly spaced posts; layered green hill bands; red bodies with white heads at the fence line; scrub dots and a dirt trail in the foreground
identifications.moreCertain: Size. At the size handed over, the cattle are three red specks and the fence is a line - the strip reads as generic green hills until enlarged. A viewer at normal size would not see livestock here

identifications.answer: A coastal lighthouse: a white tapered tower, octagonal in section, with a red lantern room and roof, a dark gallery railing below the lantern, small dark windows up the shaft and a low white service shed against its base. The classic Atlantic Canadian white-and-red light. I cannot say which lighthouse - it is drawn in isolation with no rock, sea or shore.
identifications.cues: Tapered white tower with a distinct batter; red polygonal lantern housing with a finial; railed gallery; vertical slit windows; attached single-storey shed at the foot
identifications.moreCertain: The setting. On bare granite it would read as one particular famous light; on a pier or a sandy point it would read as another. Isolated on blank ground it can only be 'a lighthouse'

identifications.answer: The Canadian Museum for Human Rights in Winnipeg. A curved glass shell - the Cloud - wrapping the left side, angular pale limestone masses rising behind it as the Mountain, and a tall tapering spire with a latticed mast on top standing for the Tower of Hope, all on a low landscaped base. Reasonably confident from the massing, though the spire is drawn more like a derrick than the glass tower it should be.
identifications.cues: Curved glazed prow with fine mullion lines sweeping up the left flank; faceted stone volumes stepping down to the right; single tall spire rising off-centre from the roof; diagonal dark window slots cut across the stone
identifications.moreCertain: The building's other side - the Cloud wraps much further round in reality - and a glass spire rather than a steel lattice. The silhouette is right but the tower detail is what makes me hold back

identifications.answer: An upright cartoon beaver, the same character as elsewhere in this set - but in THIS image the flat paddle tail is not present, and a hard-edged rectangular notch has been cut out of the body at the left hip and arm, leaving a straight vertical edge where fur should be. I still read it as a beaver from the buck teeth, muzzle and body, but I am naming what is actually on screen: no tail, and a squared bite taken out of the silhouette.
identifications.cues: Two large front incisors and cream muzzle; brown barrel body with cream belly; small round ear. Absent or cut: the paddle tail entirely, and the outline between hip and forearm, which ends in a clean right angle
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the missing tail is the asset or the hand-off. If a part of this picture was deliberately painted over, this is that image; if not, the beaver is shipping without its most identifying feature. I cannot tell which from here, and I will not report a tail I cannot see

identifications.answer: A stainless-steel dome observation car from a streamlined passenger train: fluted silver car body with a blue stripe above the window line, a long row of square windows, a raised glazed dome cupola on the roof, a red marker light at the leading end, two four-wheel trucks and a vestibule and diaphragm at the right-hand end. The classic Budd-built dome car of a transcontinental train.
identifications.cues: Roof-mounted glass observation dome, which almost nothing but a dome car has; fluted stainless side panels below the windows; blue letterboard stripe; corrugated diaphragm connector at the car end
identifications.moreCertain: Reporting marks, a railway name on the letterboard, or the bullet-nosed tail of a park car. Without lettering it is a dome car in general rather than a particular train

identifications.answer: A farmers' market produce stall drawn large: a wooden trestle counter under a green-and-white striped awning with a scalloped valance on two posts, three crates on the counter holding red apples or tomatoes, tan roots or potatoes and green cabbages, a hessian sack and a basket at the left, a dark crate under the table and two full sacks at the right.
identifications.cues: Scalloped green and white market awning; open trestle counter on posts; produce as grouped round forms in slatted wooden crates; sacks and a basket on the ground either side
identifications.moreCertain: A vendor behind the counter, or signage. The stall is clearly a market stall; what is sold is legible only as apples, roots and cabbages by colour

identifications.answer: A cable-stayed bridge crossing a river: one tall white pylon with a fan of stay cables running down to a pale deck, dark blue water beneath, and tan banks or approach piers at either end. Drawn very small. A cable-stayed road bridge - nothing here names it.
identifications.cues: Single off-centre pylon with a symmetrical cable fan - cable-stayed rather than suspension, where the cables would hang from a main catenary; thin horizontal deck line; blue water band; sandy abutments
identifications.moreCertain: A second pylon, the shoreline it lands on, or traffic for scale. At this size the deck is three pixels deep and the whole bridge is a white spike over a blue band

identifications.answer: A modern low-floor articulated tram or light-rail vehicle standing on track: red body with a black window band running its length, a raked cab end with a windscreen, articulation joints, doors between the sections, and a grey rail strip underneath. Reads as a present-day city streetcar. I cannot name the operator, though red with a black band is the common Canadian livery.
identifications.cues: Continuous dark glazing band against a red body; low-floor profile sitting close to the rail; multiple body sections with concertina joints; single-ended cab with a sloped screen
identifications.moreCertain: A route number, roof pantograph or fleet lettering. At this size the pantograph and pole are not visible at all, which is most of what would say tram rather than bus

identifications.answer: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer in Red Serge full dress: scarlet tunic, tan flat-brimmed Stetson campaign hat, brown Sam Browne belt with the cross strap over the right shoulder, dark blue breeches with a yellow leg stripe, brown high riding boots, and long dark hair worn down. A woman officer in ceremonial order. Confident.
identifications.cues: The combination is unmistakable - scarlet tunic plus tan Stetson plus Sam Browne cross strap plus yellow-striped blue breeches plus brown riding boots; brass belt buckle; white lanyard across the chest
identifications.moreCertain: Collar or shoulder badges would confirm the force rather than the look. One quibble: the hair hangs loose down the back, where the dress standard would have it up under the Stetson

identifications.answer: Two cartoon characters standing apart, facing each other: on the left a person with dark curly hair and brown skin in a blue winter parka with a red scarf, red mitten, grey trousers and brown boots; on the right an RCMP officer in Red Serge - scarlet tunic, tan Stetson, Sam Browne cross strap, blue breeches with a yellow stripe, brown riding boots - with blonde hair and a smile. Same two roles as another image in this set, cast with different skin and hair.
identifications.cues: Mountie: scarlet tunic, tan Stetson, cross strap, yellow-striped breeches, riding boots. Civilian: parka, scarf, mittens - dressed for winter. Both outlined, identical cartoon proportions
identifications.moreCertain: The Mountie is clear. The civilian is only 'someone in a winter coat' - no tool, badge or bag says what they do

identifications.answer: A railway freight car on track carrying intermodal containers: a grey flat or well car on two trucks, with a blue container sitting in the well and a rust-red container stacked on top of it, running on rails with brown sleepers. A double-stacked container car.
identifications.cues: Corrugated container side ribs on both boxes; the lower box sunk between the trucks, which is what makes it a well car rather than a flatcar; two-axle trucks at each end; ballasted track with sleepers
identifications.moreCertain: Container markings or a railway name. Also the stacking reads slightly oddly - the upper container overhangs the lower one at both ends rather than sitting flush inside the stacking castings

identifications.answer: A frozen canal being skated on in winter - a public skateway. A concrete road bridge on two piers crosses the back with a balustrade and lamp standards along it, snowy banks with small spruce run below, a timber warming hut with a snow-laden roof sits on the bank, and five or six figures in coloured winter coats are skating on the pale blue ice in proper skating poses, leaning into the stride with one leg trailing. Most likely the Rideau Canal Skateway in Ottawa, though nothing here names it.
identifications.cues: Long straight ice surface between built banks; warming hut beside the ice, which is specific to a maintained skateway; skaters in mid-stride with trailing legs and blades; road bridge with lamps crossing overhead; snow drifts and spruce on the banks
identifications.moreCertain: A landmark on the skyline. Also worth recording: at the size handed over this reads as a pale blue band and I had to enlarge it before any of the skaters or the hut were visible at all

identifications.answer: A sternwheel paddle steamer - a river steamboat with a big wooden paddlewheel at the stern, three white decks of cabin windows, a tall buff funnel, a pilothouse on the top deck, and king posts with spars and hog chains along the superstructure. The classic inland riverboat. I cannot name the vessel.
identifications.cues: Large spoked timber paddlewheel carried at the stern rather than at the sides; stacked white cabin decks with rows of small square windows; single funnel; spar and hog-chain rig over the roof, which is what holds a shallow-draught hull straight
identifications.moreCertain: A name board on the wheelhouse or the hull, and the river around it. The type is unmistakable, the individual boat is not

identifications.answer: An oil pumpjack - a nodding-donkey beam pump on a wellsite: red counterweight crank and red horsehead at the end of the walking beam, white Samson post A-frame, a red access ladder, black gearbox and prime mover on a skid, and a small wellhead with a valve wheel at the right, all on a green grass pad.
identifications.cues: Horsehead curving over the wellhead on a pivoted walking beam - the defining shape; A-frame Samson post beneath the pivot; counterweighted crank at the rear; separate wellhead with a hand valve
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing much - the machine is unambiguous. Scale against a truck or a tank battery would help place it in a field rather than in isolation

identifications.answer: A short run of farm fence with a gate: round timber posts carrying four horizontal rails or wires, and a braced wooden five-bar gate with a diagonal brace hung between two heavier posts, standing on a strip of green grass. A field or paddock gate - nothing more specific.
identifications.cues: Regularly spaced round posts; horizontal rail lines; gate with a corner-to-corner diagonal brace, which is how a real gate is kept from sagging; grass ground strip
identifications.moreCertain: Context - stock behind it, a track through it, a farmyard. On its own it is a fence section, which may be all it is meant to be

identifications.answer: A person riding a bicycle in profile facing right: a silver-grey cycling helmet, a blue coat over a red top, red gloves on the handlebars, brown boots on the pedals, on a red-framed bicycle with white-walled tyres. A everyday cyclist, helmeted.
identifications.cues: Bicycle in clean side view with both wheels, chainset and handlebars; rider seated with hands on the bars and a foot on each pedal; helmet on the head; coat and gloves suggesting cold weather riding
identifications.moreCertain: The far leg and far arm are hard to separate from the near ones, so the pedalling pose is a little ambiguous; clearer limb separation would settle whether this is mid-stroke or static. The rider's lower body also reads as a single blue mass where the coat meets the leg

identifications.answer: An upright cartoon beaver standing in three-quarter view - brown fur, cream belly and muzzle, two large front incisors, small round ear, and the broad flat cross-hatched paddle tail present and visible behind the left leg. The same beaver character as elsewhere in this set, here complete with its tail.
identifications.cues: Buck incisors and cream muzzle; barrel body with cream belly panel; small high round ear; flat scaly paddle tail resting on the ground behind; short clawed feet
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the animal. The far arm still merges into the body silhouette, which is the one place the pose goes soft

identifications.answer: A farm fence with a hung gate, drawn large: pale timber posts carrying four grey horizontal rails, and between two darker heavier posts a five-bar wooden gate with a diagonal brace and dark metal hinge straps, standing on a green grass bank. A paddock or field gate.
identifications.cues: Diagonal brace running corner to corner across the gate, the correct way a gate is braced; dark hinge plates on the hanging post; capped post tops; grass strip with tufts at the post feet
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to identify it - it is plainly a gate. What it is a gate to would need the field or yard behind it

identifications.answer: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer in Red Serge: scarlet tunic, tan flat-brimmed Stetson, brown Sam Browne belt with cross strap, blue breeches with a yellow leg stripe, brown riding boots, short curly brown hair. Same role as another figure in this set, cast with different hair and skin tone.
identifications.cues: Scarlet tunic with the Sam Browne cross strap and brass buckle; tan Stetson with a flat brim; yellow-striped dark blue breeches; tall brown boots; white lanyard
identifications.moreCertain: Badges or collar insignia would confirm the force outright rather than by uniform convention

identifications.answer: An oil pumpjack on a wellsite, drawn large: red horsehead on a walking beam pivoted on a white A-frame Samson post, red counterweight crank at the rear, black gearbox and motor on a skid, a red ladder up the frame, a polished rod and stuffing box hanging from the horsehead into a wellhead with a valve wheel, all on a gravel pad with grass.
identifications.cues: Horsehead and bridle hanging over the wellhead; walking beam on a central pivot; counterweight crank; separate wellhead with a hand valve and Christmas-tree fitting; gravel lease pad
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. The machine is drawn with the right parts in the right relationship and reads immediately

identifications.answer: The same city waterfront park strip as elsewhere in this set, shown at its smallest: a paved terrace with lamps and benches, three round-crowned trees - two autumn orange, one green - a pale water band, and a row of grey and blue towers behind. At this size the people are single pixels and the street furniture has all but vanished; it reads as three trees against a generic skyline.
identifications.cues: Three lollipop tree crowns; flat grey skyline bars with blue accents; horizontal banded terrace; no legible figures
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing would make the city identifiable - it is anonymous at every size. What this smallest render shows is that the park loses its people and benches entirely, leaving only trees and boxes

identifications.answer: A wooden prairie grain elevator: a tall square cribbed timber tower in oxblood red with a gabled roof, a small cupola head house with a vent stack on top, a long low annex sloping away to the left, a loading spout or manlift leg angled down the right side, small square windows up the tower, and railway track running along the base. The classic Prairie grain elevator and it reads immediately.
identifications.cues: Tall square tower with a pitched roof and a cupola - the elevator leg housing; low annex shed attached along one side; spout arm reaching down to trackside; siding track at the foot; yellow trim picking out the eaves
identifications.moreCertain: The company name painted across the tower and the town name beneath it, which is how these are actually read at a distance. The structure is right; it is anonymous

identifications.answer: A small single-storey cabin in winter: brown board or log walls, a wide low-pitched roof carrying snow with deep eaves, two windows lit warm yellow, a dark plank door in the middle, a log pile or bench under the left window, a small spruce at the right, standing on pale blue ice or packed snow. Reads as a warming hut or winter cabin.
identifications.cues: Snow load along the roof ridge and eaves; windows glowing yellow against a dark interior, which says occupied and heated; pale blue-white ground rather than earth; spruce beside the door
identifications.moreCertain: Whether it sits on ice or on land - the ground is drawn as pale blue with lighter streaks, which could be a frozen surface or just snow. A skate rack or a stove pipe would settle what the hut is for

identifications.answer: The same wooden prairie grain elevator as another image in this set, shown smaller: oxblood red cribbed tower with a gabled roof and vent cupola, yellow eave trim, a long annex sloping away to the left, a spout arm down the right side and track at the base. Still clearly an elevator at this size.
identifications.cues: Tall square tower with cupola against a low sloping annex - the elevator profile survives the reduction; yellow trim lines; grey track strip at the foot
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for identification. The silhouette is strong enough that this reads at small size, which is more than some other assets in this set manage

identifications.answer: I cannot tell. This is the same object as another image in this set, drawn slightly larger, and it is still entirely in flat greys and beiges: two long tapering bars lying roughly parallel with dark round caps at their ends, a pale flat platform beneath them, a small cluster of three or four short prongs standing up near the middle-left, and a dark ground strip. Nothing reads as a recognisable object. Best guesses remain a sled, a cart or a low machine, none of which I would defend.
identifications.cues: Paired long members with capped ends; flat platform below; small pronged upright cluster; total absence of colour or marking; no wheels, seat, handle or opening that would name the type
identifications.moreCertain: Colour and any internal detail. Seeing it twice at two sizes and getting nowhere both times is itself the finding: whatever this is meant to be, it does not communicate at any size handed over

identifications.answer: A police officer in Red Serge - scarlet tunic, Sam Browne belt with cross strap and brass buckle, dark blue breeches with a yellow leg stripe, brown riding boots, white lanyard - but bare-headed, with short curly brown hair and NO Stetson. Everything except the hat matches the Mounted Police figures elsewhere in this set. I am naming what is on screen: the campaign hat is absent.
identifications.cues: Present: scarlet tunic, cross strap, yellow-striped blue breeches, brown boots, lanyard. Absent: the tan flat-brimmed Stetson that the other figures in this uniform wear
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the missing hat is the asset or a deliberately painted-over probe. Without the Stetson the uniform still reads as ceremonial police, but the single most recognisable element of the look is gone, and I will not report a hat I cannot see

identifications.answer: A canal lock with closed mitre gates, at a middling size: two gate leaves meeting at a centre post in a shallow V, coursed stone chamber walls either side, dark railings on the wall tops, and water below. Same lock as other images in this set.
identifications.cues: Mitre pair of gate leaves; ashlar block walls; railed copings; horizontal strapping bands on the gates; small dark fitting at the gate head
identifications.moreCertain: Balance beams, a lock-keeper or a boat in the chamber. As drawn the lock is correct but static and unpeopled, so nothing says it works

identifications.answer: The corner of a masonry wall in winter: pale tan dressed stone blocks in courses, returning around a corner so two faces show, with a brown coping band and a cap of snow along the top and a drift of snow at the foot. A fragment of stonework - I cannot say what structure it belongs to.
identifications.cues: Coursed ashlar blocks with drawn joint lines on both faces; the corner return giving it depth; snow cap on the coping and a curved drift at the base; no opening, roof or feature
identifications.moreCertain: Almost anything else - a roofline, a door, a window, the rest of the building. This is a wall corner and nothing in it says whether it is a lock, a rampart, a foundation or a garden wall

identifications.answer: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer in Red Serge, shown small: tan Stetson, scarlet tunic, Sam Browne cross strap, yellow-striped blue breeches, brown riding boots. Same figure as elsewhere in this set at a reduced size; the uniform still reads.
identifications.cues: Tan flat-brimmed hat plus scarlet tunic plus yellow leg stripe - the three cues that survive shrinking; cross strap still visible as a diagonal; boots as dark blocks
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. This is the size test and the figure passes it - the silhouette and the colour blocking keep the role legible

identifications.answer: A polygonal Gothic Revival building with a steep conical roof - tan sandstone walls divided by buttresses, tall pointed arched windows between them, a ring of small gabled dormers around the base of the roof, a dark slate spire and a finial on top, standing in snow. This reads to me as the Library of Parliament in Ottawa, the round chapter-house block behind Centre Block, though I hold that loosely.
identifications.cues: Sixteen-sided drum plan implied by the angled faces and buttresses; tall lancet windows; dormered conical roof with a crowning finial; honey sandstone with grey slate - the Ottawa Parliamentary palette
identifications.moreCertain: The flying buttresses and the connecting corridor to Centre Block, which are what make the Library unmistakable. Drawn in isolation on snow, this could be a chapter house, a rotunda or a large bandstand

identifications.answer: A coastal lighthouse drawn large: white tapered tower with a pronounced batter, a red-painted lantern room with glazing bars and a ball finial, a dark railed gallery on a white corbelled platform, three slit windows up the shaft, and a low white service shed with a dark door at the base. The standard white-tower, red-lantern light. No setting, so I cannot name it.
identifications.cues: Battered white tower; red polygonal lantern housing with finial; gallery railing on a projecting platform; staggered vertical windows; attached keeper's shed
identifications.moreCertain: The rock, sea or shoreline it stands on. The tower is well drawn and reads instantly as a lighthouse; what it cannot do in isolation is be a particular one

identifications.answer: A railway lineside background strip: two tracks on ballast with sleepers and rails running the full width, a level-crossing signal beside the line with a white X crossbuck and two red lamps on a mast, four timber telegraph or power poles with crossarms and sagging wires, a post-and-wire boundary fence, and fields and hedgerows behind in green and tan. A rural railway crossing.
identifications.cues: Crossbuck X with paired red lights - the standard level-crossing signal; ballast shoulder and sleeper spacing; telegraph poles with insulators and catenary-like wires; lineside fence separating track from field
identifications.moreCertain: A road actually crossing the track. The signal implies a crossing but no roadway is drawn meeting the rails, so the sign stands in a field

identifications.answer: The same small winter cabin as elsewhere in this set, shown smaller: brown boarded walls, wide snow-covered roof, two yellow-lit windows, dark door, a spruce at the right, on pale blue ice or snow. Still legible as a lit hut in winter.
identifications.cues: Warm yellow window blocks against dark walls - the strongest cue at this size; snow line along the roof; small dark conifer beside it
identifications.moreCertain: The same ambiguity as at full size: whether the pale blue ground is ice or snow, which decides whether this is a hut on a frozen waterway or a cabin in a snowy yard

identifications.answer: The same farm fence and braced gate as elsewhere in this set, at a middling size: pale posts with grey horizontal rails, a braced wooden gate hung between two darker posts with dark hinges, on a green grass strip.
identifications.cues: Diagonal gate brace; capped posts; four rail lines; grass base strip
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for identification - it is a gate at every size. The brace and hinges survive the reduction, which is the useful part

identifications.answer: A single cartoon figure dressed for winter, standing facing forward: brown skin, short blond curly hair, a blue parka with white cuffs, a red scarf hanging down the front, a red mitten at the left hand, grey trousers with white bands above brown boots. A civilian in cold-weather clothing - no role marker of any kind.
identifications.cues: Parka, scarf, mitten and boots; arms hanging straight at the sides; outlined cartoon style with three-tone shading; neutral standing pose
identifications.moreCertain: Anything that says who this person is. As a 'winter civilian' it reads fine; if it is meant to be a specific role - a guide, a worker, a student - nothing on the figure carries that. The arms also hang almost perfectly vertical with very little shoulder shape

identifications.answer: A white colonial-style civic building with a clock tower: a long two-storey white block with a dark hipped roof and tall sash windows on a stone basement with an arched opening, a columned portico rising through the middle, a square clock stage above it with a deep blue dial and gold hands, an open bell chamber holding two gold bells, and a green copper dome capped with a gold ball, on a green lawn. A town hall, courthouse or legislature of the British colonial tradition. I cannot name it with confidence - the Halifax Old Town Clock is the nearest thing that comes to mind, but this has a much larger building under it than that does.
identifications.cues: Green copper dome with gold finial; blue clock face with gilt hands; open arcaded belfry with visible bells; white classical portico with slender columns; symmetrical Georgian fenestration; rusticated stone base
identifications.moreCertain: The setting - a hill, a parade ground, a street - and the building's plan. The elements are those of several different colonial landmarks and nothing here picks one out

identifications.answer: A broadleaf tree in autumn colour: a rounded canopy built from overlapping lobes in orange, rust and deep maroon, a short brown trunk, and a scatter of fallen leaves on the ground around it. The fallen leaves are drawn as pointed star shapes with several lobes, which reads as maple. So: a maple in autumn.
identifications.cues: Three-tone autumn canopy - bright orange lit side, mid rust, dark maroon shadow; multi-lobed pointed leaf shapes on the ground, the giveaway for maple; stubby trunk and a dark earth collar at the base
identifications.moreCertain: Leaf shape in the canopy itself. The crown is drawn as plain blobs, so the maple reading rests entirely on five or six small fallen leaves at the foot - at a smaller size that cue would disappear and this would just be an orange tree

identifications.answer: The Centre Block of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa, with the Peace Tower. Honey sandstone Gothic Revival frontage with a long ranked row of pointed arch windows, a green copper roof with dormers, corner pavilions with green pyramidal caps, a tall central clock tower with a white clock face and a green copper spire, the arched main entrance beneath it, a dark secondary spire to the right, and a line of evergreens along the front lawn. Confident.
identifications.cues: Peace Tower proportions - tall square shaft, clock stage, tapering green spire; Gothic lancet window arcade across the whole facade; green copper roofing against buff sandstone, the Parliament Hill palette; symmetrical corner towers
identifications.moreCertain: The flag on the tower and the Library's round block at the rear would clinch it. The clock face is also drawn plain white with simple hands where the real one is more detailed, but the silhouette is right

identifications.answer: The same stainless-steel dome observation car as elsewhere in this set, shown smaller: fluted silver carbody with a blue stripe, a row of windows, the raised glass dome on the roof, a red marker light at the leading end, trucks and an end vestibule. Still reads as a dome car.
identifications.cues: Roof dome breaking the roofline; blue letterboard stripe; fluted stainless sides; two trucks and a vestibule at the end
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the type. The dome survives shrinking, which is the thing that matters - it is the one feature that separates this from any other coach

identifications.answer: A small detached suburban house: cream or pale yellow siding, a blue-grey pitched roof, a red brick chimney, two upper windows and two lower windows with white frames, a pale front door reached by steps, clipped green shrubs either side, a low white picket fence, and a green lawn with small red flowers. An ordinary family home.
identifications.cues: Gable roof with a chimney; symmetrical window arrangement around a central door; front path and steps; foundation planting and picket fence - the standard suburban house vocabulary
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to identify the type. If it is meant to be a particular regional house form - a Maritime saltbox, a Quebec farmhouse, a prairie foursquare - none of those is legible here; it is a generic house

identifications.answer: I am not confident. A large grey-beige dome with a smaller dome beside it to the right, both sitting on a dark plinth, with a dark arched band curving across the big dome and a vertical dark strip running up to it, a blue oval pool in front with pale blue streaks, and a few small green shrubs. My best reading is a snow house - a dome with a smaller entrance dome - but it is drawn in flat greys and beiges with no white and no block coursing, and the pool in front fits a building rather than an igloo. Second reading: a domed arena or planetarium with a reflecting pool.
identifications.cues: Two domes of unequal size side by side; arched dark band reading as an entrance or a seam; oval blue pool with highlight lines; green shrubs as the only saturated colour in the image
identifications.moreCertain: Colour. Everything here is one desaturated grey-beige family, which is the second object in this hand-off with that problem. Snow blocks, white, or any surface marking would settle it instantly; as drawn I cannot say whether this is a building or a dwelling

identifications.answer: A cable-stayed bridge, drawn larger: a single tall white pylon leaning slightly, with a fan of pale stay cables running down to a white deck on both sides, a dark blue band beneath carrying thin light-blue lines, and a brown banded strip along the bottom with regular vertical divisions - reading as the water and then a shore or a lower approach structure. A modern cable-stayed span; nothing names it.
identifications.cues: Single pylon with a symmetrical cable fan - cable-stayed, not suspension; thin white deck line crossing the full width; dark blue water band; regularly divided brown band beneath
identifications.moreCertain: What the brown band at the bottom is - it could be a pier, a wharf or a bank, and it sits below the water band, which is confusing. A second pylon or an anchorage would also help; the span is cut off at both edges

identifications.answer: A maple tree in autumn, drawn large: a billowing canopy of overlapping lobes in bright orange, rust red and deep maroon, a tapering brown trunk, a dark earth collar at its foot, and six fallen leaves scattered on the ground drawn clearly as multi-pointed maple leaves. At this size the maple reading is firm.
identifications.cues: Distinctly maple-shaped fallen leaves with pointed lobes; three-tone autumn canopy with a lit side, a mid tone and a shadow side; rounded cloud-lobe crown; short sturdy trunk
identifications.moreCertain: Maple leaf shapes in the crown itself rather than only on the ground. The canopy is built from plain circles, so the species is carried entirely by the litter at the base

identifications.answer: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer in Red Serge at small size: tan Stetson, scarlet tunic with cross strap and belt, blue breeches with a yellow stripe, brown riding boots, long dark hair. The uniform still reads clearly.
identifications.cues: Tan hat, red tunic and yellow leg stripe hold up as colour blocks; diagonal cross strap still visible; dark hair against the red
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - this passes the size test. Same note as the larger version: the hair is worn loose rather than up under the Stetson

identifications.answer: The winter-dressed civilian figure at small size: brown skin, short blond curly hair, navy parka with white cuffs, red scarf down the front, a red mitten, grey trousers, brown boots. Reads as a person in winter clothing and nothing more specific.
identifications.cues: Navy coat mass with the red scarf as the one strong accent; white cuff bands; boots as brown blocks; straight-down arms
identifications.moreCertain: A role marker. At this size the figure is a blue silhouette with a red stripe - if it is meant to be anyone in particular, that does not survive the reduction, and it did not read at full size either

identifications.answer: The Centre Block of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa with the Peace Tower, shown small and flying the Canadian flag from the tower. Sandstone Gothic Revival frontage, green copper roofs and corner turrets, arcade of pointed windows, central clock tower with a green spire, the Library's dark spire behind to the right, evergreens along the front.
identifications.cues: Peace Tower silhouette with clock and green spire; maple-leaf flag flying above it, which fixes the country outright; green copper roof against buff stone; Gothic window arcade
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - the flag plus the tower makes this the most decisively identified building in the set, and it holds up at this reduced size

identifications.answer: A winter-dressed figure - dark skin, long blonde hair, blue coat, red scarf, red mitten, grey trousers - sitting on a wooden sled with an upcurved front runner, leaning back with one mittened hand down behind. Larger than the other version of this pose in the set, and now clearer: it is a person on a sled rather than a skater. The pose still reads badly - the figure looks to be tipping over backwards rather than riding, the torso is pitched back past balance, and a grey wedge shape at the right leg does not resolve into either a boot or a blade.
identifications.cues: Wooden sled with upturned curved runner and a flat slat deck; seated figure with legs forward; mittened hand planted behind; winter coat and scarf
identifications.moreCertain: What the grey wedge at the right foot is meant to be. If these figures are supposed to be skating - and other winter art in this set shows proper skaters - then this pose is wrong for it. If they are sledding, the balance is still off

identifications.answer: The upright cartoon beaver at small size: brown fur, cream belly and muzzle, front teeth, small round ear, flat cross-hatched paddle tail behind. Still reads as a beaver.
identifications.cues: Paddle tail and buck teeth both survive the reduction; cream belly panel against brown fur; stocky upright stance
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. The two features that make a beaver a beaver - tail and teeth - are still legible here, which is the point of the small size

identifications.answer: The upright cartoon beaver again - brown fur, cream belly, small round ear, flat cross-hatched paddle tail present - but in THIS image the mouth and front teeth are covered by a plain pale rectangle laid over the muzzle. The incisors are not visible. I still read the animal as a beaver, but from the tail, body shape and ear, NOT from the teeth, because the teeth are painted out here.
identifications.cues: Present: paddle tail with cross-hatching, cream belly, round ear, stocky upright body. Obscured: the muzzle and both incisors, hidden behind a flat light-coloured box with hard straight edges that belongs to no part of the drawing
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing would change my reading - the tail alone carries it. Recording plainly: this render does not show the beaver's teeth, and I am not going to report a feature that a rectangle is sitting on top of

identifications.answer: A combine harvester working a field: red machine body with a glazed cab on top, an unloading auger arm folded out to the upper left, large drive wheels and smaller steering wheels, and a tan cutting header with a reel at the front right, standing on a strip of stubble or cut crop. Drawn small.
identifications.cues: Unloading auger swung out over the side - the feature that separates a combine from a tractor; header with a reel at the front; high cab set above a bulky body; big front wheels and small rear ones
identifications.moreCertain: Size - at the scale handed over the header and reel are a few pixels of tan and the auger is a thin line. A colour or a maker's silhouette would also help but is not needed to call it a combine

identifications.answer: Three Hereford cattle on grass, drawn large: red-brown bodies with the breed's white face, white muzzle and white legs, a cow with two smaller calves stepping back behind her, dark tail switches and dark hooves. The breed marking is right, but the drawing is very simplified - the white underline is a single floating white bar laid across the legs rather than belly marking, the faces are flat white quadrilaterals, and the ears read as grey blobs.
identifications.cues: White face and stockings against a red body - Hereford; blocky beef bodies with a straight topline; three descending sizes reading as cow and calves; tail with a dark switch
identifications.moreCertain: Muzzle, eye and ear drawn as recognisable features rather than flat shapes. The animal reads as cattle immediately but does not bear close looking at - the heads in particular are the weakest part

identifications.answer: Four hopper-bottom grain storage bins on a concrete pad, drawn large: tan-grey cylinders with horizontal ring seams, peaked conical roofs each with a small cap vent, a blue access ladder up the second bin, and cone bottoms carried on slim steel legs with discharge spouts beneath. Farm grain bins - not a wooden elevator.
identifications.cues: Conical hopper bottoms on legs with spouts underneath, which is bin construction; ring seams up the walls; peaked roofs with vent caps; ladder; poured pad with tie-down marks
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the type. Worth noting the colour: these are drawn in flat grey-tan with very little saturation compared with the rest of the set

identifications.answer: A red fishing shack or fish store on a timber wharf, drawn large: deep red board walls with white corner trim, a grey-blue gable roof, a window and a pair of red double doors facing us, a plank deck on posts with a white railed walkway running off to the left, stacks of pale teal and blue crates or traps piled under the deck edge, a grey boulder at the right and water below. A working waterfront store.
identifications.cues: Fish-store red cladding with white trim; wide double doors for gear; wharf decking on posts over water; stacked crates or lobster traps beneath; boulder and shoreline
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the teal stacks are lobster traps, crates or pallets - they are drawn as plain slatted rectangles. Traps would place this firmly on the Atlantic coast; as drawn they could be anything

identifications.answer: The CN Tower and the domed stadium beside it in Toronto - the Rogers Centre, formerly SkyDome. A tall slender concrete tower with a flared observation pod, a smaller upper pod and a long antenna mast, standing immediately behind a white retractable-roof dome on a dark colonnaded base, with a green tree and a low blue-glass building to the right. Confident.
identifications.cues: CN Tower profile - tapering shaft, main pod with a dark band and a white underside, skypod above, needle mast; the two together, tower directly behind the dome, is the Toronto waterfront view; white segmented dome roof over a ring of dark piers
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing much. The pairing of these two buildings is unique and the silhouettes are both right, even at this small size

identifications.answer: A city market street, drawn very small - I had to enlarge it to read anything. A paved street with bollards and lamp standards, a white hipped-roof civic building on the left, a covered timber market stall in the middle with a vendor in white behind a counter, trestle tables of goods, green street trees, a red-brick apartment block on the right, and a row of pale blue and stone buildings behind. Four or five shoppers stand about. A public market in a town centre.
identifications.cues: Open-fronted market stall with a vendor and counters; shoppers in groups; street trees, bollards and lamps; mixed civic and residential frontages behind
identifications.moreCertain: Size, above all. At the size handed over this strip is a smear of pale colours - the stalls, the vendor and every shopper are invisible. Nothing names the town either

identifications.answer: The same modern museum as elsewhere in this set, shown small: a curved glass shell on the left, faceted pale stone masses stepping down to the right, and a tall tapering spire with a lattice mast rising from the roof. I read it as the Canadian Museum for Human Rights in Winnipeg. At this size the glazing detail is gone and it is mostly a beige wedge with a blue spike.
identifications.cues: Curved glass prow; stone mountain massing; single off-centre spire; dark diagonal window slots
identifications.moreCertain: The spire is the only distinguishing feature left at this size, and it is drawn as a derrick-like lattice rather than the glass tower it should be, which weakens the identification exactly where it matters most

identifications.answer: The same modern museum again at a middling size - curved glazed shell wrapping the left flank, angular limestone volumes behind and to the right, dark diagonal window slots, a blue tapering spire with a grey lattice mast on top, on a brown landscaped base with green edges. My reading remains the Canadian Museum for Human Rights, Winnipeg, held loosely.
identifications.cues: Glass cloud against stone mountain; stepped faceted masses; single tall spire; diagonal glazing slots cut across the stone
identifications.moreCertain: A glass Tower of Hope instead of a steel lattice, and more of the glass wrapping visible. The massing is convincing; the tower detail is what keeps me from calling it outright

identifications.answer: The same white colonial civic building with a clock tower as elsewhere in this set, shown small: long white block with a dark hipped roof, columned portico, blue clock face, arcaded belfry with gold bells, green copper dome with a gold finial, on a green lawn. A town hall, courthouse or colonial legislature - still not one I can name.
identifications.cues: Green dome over a white classical body; blue clock dial; belfry arches; regular dark window blocks
identifications.moreCertain: The same as at full size: a setting, or the building's plan. The parts are generic colonial-Georgian and no single feature picks out a particular landmark

identifications.answer: The upright cartoon beaver at small size, complete: brown fur, cream belly and muzzle, visible front teeth, small round ear, flat cross-hatched paddle tail behind the leg.
identifications.cues: Paddle tail; buck teeth; cream belly panel; upright stocky stance
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - the beaver reads at this size

identifications.answer: A railway freight car carrying two stacked intermodal containers, drawn large: a grey flat deck car on two four-wheel trucks, a blue ribbed container sitting on the deck and a rust-red ribbed container stacked on top of it, running on ballasted track with brown sleepers. A double-stack container car.
identifications.cues: Two corrugated container boxes stacked; grey car deck and side sills; two trucks with two axles each; sleepered track beneath
identifications.moreCertain: The stacking is not quite right - both containers overhang the car deck at each end and the lower one sits on top of the deck rather than down in a well, which is what a real double-stack car uses. A railway or container marking would also place it

identifications.answer: Three Hereford cattle on grass at small size - red-brown bodies, white faces and white legs, a cow with two smaller calves behind. Still reads as white-faced cattle.
identifications.cues: White face against red body survives the reduction; three descending sizes; green grass strip
identifications.moreCertain: The heads are now three white specks - the breed reading is carried entirely by the face colour, which is at least the right cue to survive

identifications.answer: A grand railway chateau hotel: warm orange-brown masonry, symmetrical wings, steep dark slate roofs with green copper sections and rows of dormers, corner turrets with conical caps, and a tall central tower with a steep pitched roof and a finial, with a line of evergreens along the front. This is the Canadian chateau-style hotel type, and my best guess is the Chateau Frontenac at Quebec City - though the Chateau Laurier in Ottawa and the Banff Springs Hotel share the same vocabulary and I cannot separate them from this view.
identifications.cues: Chateauesque massing - steep roofs, dormers, round corner turrets with candle-snuffer caps; a dominant central tower; green copper roofing against warm stone; symmetrical flanking wings
identifications.moreCertain: The setting. Frontenac sits on a cliff above the St Lawrence with a terrace, Laurier sits beside a canal and Parliament, Banff Springs sits in mountains. Drawn on blank ground, the type is obvious and the individual hotel is not

identifications.answer: The same frozen canal scene as earlier in this set, at a smaller size: stone embankment with a green iron railing, globe lamps, benches, a warming shelter, a heavy timber trestle frame at the left, and three small figures out on the pale ice sitting on sleds. Reads as a frozen urban canal used for winter recreation.
identifications.cues: Walled straight ice channel; period railing and lamps along the bank; shelter and benches; seated figures on the ice
identifications.moreCertain: The same two gaps as at full size: nothing names the city, and the figures on the ice are seated sledders rather than skaters, which leaves the scene saying something different from the other winter-canal art in this set

identifications.answer: The wooden prairie grain elevator again, smaller: red cribbed tower with a gabled roof and vent cupola, yellow eave trim, low annex sloping to the left, spout arm on the right, track along the base.
identifications.cues: Tower-and-annex silhouette; cupola on the ridge; yellow trim; trackside strip
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - the elevator silhouette is strong and survives the size ladder well

identifications.answer: The same northern shoreline background strip as earlier, smaller: dark spruce treeline on a sandy bank, a wide pale turquoise water band, and a grey cobble foreground with low green shrubs and yellow flowers. A generic boreal lake or river shore.
identifications.cues: Banded horizontal composition; sawtooth conifer skyline; flat turquoise water with ripple dashes; grey cobbles and yellow flower dots
identifications.moreCertain: Any landform or built feature. It is an unnamed northern shoreline at every size in this set

identifications.answer: The Centre Block of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa with the Peace Tower, flying the Canadian flag. Sandstone Gothic Revival frontage with a pointed-window arcade, green copper roofs and corner turrets, central clock tower with green spire, the Library's dark spire behind to the right, evergreens along the front.
identifications.cues: Peace Tower with clock and green spire; maple-leaf flag above it; green copper roofline over buff stone; Gothic arcade
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - flag plus tower is decisive and holds at this size

identifications.answer: A bulk carrier freighter alongside: long dark red hull with a flare at the bow, a white multi-deck superstructure and bridge set well forward, a red funnel with a black cap, a mast, and four deck cranes or unloading booms ranged along the long open hatch deck, floating on blue water with a brown quay or shore band below. The forward-superstructure profile is characteristic of a Great Lakes laker.
identifications.cues: Accommodation block and funnel placed at the bow end rather than aft; long flush hatch deck with self-unloading booms; deep red hull with a boot topping; four cranes evenly spaced
identifications.moreCertain: A name or a stack marking, and whether the boom at the stern is a self-unloader. The forward bridge is a strong hint of a laker but the hull could be an ocean bulker drawn loosely

identifications.answer: A winter-dressed civilian figure wearing a red knitted hat with a bobble on top - a toque - along with a navy parka, red scarf, red mitten, grey trousers with white cuffs and brown boots. Pale skin, brown hair showing under the hat. Same civilian role as the other winter figures in this set, this one with a hat.
identifications.cues: Knitted toque with a pompom, the one new element here; parka, scarf and mitten; boots; straight-armed standing pose; outlined cartoon style
identifications.moreCertain: A role marker. The toque is a nice specific touch of cold-weather dress, but the figure is still 'a person dressed for winter' with nothing saying who they are

identifications.answer: The stainless-steel dome observation car at its smallest: silver carbody with a blue stripe and window row, the raised dome still breaking the roofline, trucks and an end vestibule. Reads as a dome car even here.
identifications.cues: Roof dome silhouette; blue stripe; long low silver body; two trucks
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing - the dome is the identifying feature and it is the last thing to survive, which is the right outcome

identifications.answer: The red barn with its paddock and white horse, shown smaller: red gabled barn with white trim and a roof cupola, an open stable wing with a window band, a post-and-rail paddock on sandy ground, and a white horse standing in it. The barn reads well; the horse is still the weak part - at this size it is a pale angular blob with a wedge for a head, and it reads more like a goat or a carved figure than a horse.
identifications.cues: Barn: red cladding, cupola, sliding door, lean-to stable wing. Paddock: timber posts and rails. Horse: white, faceted, stiff-legged
identifications.moreCertain: The horse needs redrawing rather than more information. Everything else in the picture holds up at this size; the animal does not

identifications.answer: The Centre Block of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa with the Peace Tower, drawn large and flying the Canadian flag. Buff sandstone Gothic Revival frontage with a long arcade of pointed windows, green copper roof with chimneys and dormers, corner pavilions with green pyramid caps, central clock tower with a white dial and green spire, arched main entrance below, the Library's dark spire behind to the right, evergreens along the terrace.
identifications.cues: Peace Tower silhouette with clock stage and tapering green spire; maple-leaf flag flying from it; Gothic lancet arcade across the facade; green copper against buff stone
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. This is the most clearly identifiable landmark in the hand-off and it reads instantly

identifications.answer: The same town market street as elsewhere in this set, at a middling size: a white hipped-roof civic building, a covered timber market stall with a vendor, trestle tables, green street trees, lamp standards and bollards, a red-brick block on the right and pale buildings behind, with a handful of shoppers on the pavement.
identifications.cues: Market stall with counter and vendor; groups of small figures; street trees and lamps; mixed building frontages
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing names the town. The stall and figures are legible at this size, which they were not at the smallest

identifications.answer: A broken figure. The upper part is a Red Serge police officer - tan Stetson, scarlet tunic, Sam Browne cross strap and brass buckle, white lanyard, curly brown hair - drawn down to about the waist, where the body simply stops on a straight horizontal edge. Below that is empty background, and then, floating well beneath with a clear gap between, a pair of brown riding boots on their own. The breeches, legs and hips are entirely absent. Whatever this was meant to be, as rendered it is a torso and a pair of disconnected boots.
identifications.cues: Present: Stetson, scarlet tunic, cross strap, belt, lanyard, and separately a pair of riding boots with yellow trim. Missing: everything between the belt and the boot tops - no legs, no breeches, no hips. The torso ends in a hard straight cut and the boots sit in mid-air with their own cast shadow
identifications.moreCertain: Whether this is a deliberate cut-out probe or a genuinely broken rig. Either way the figure as shown is not whole, and I am recording it as broken rather than quietly reading a Mountie into the gap

identifications.answer: A polygonal Gothic Revival building with a steep conical roof, drawn large: honey sandstone faces divided by buttresses, tall pointed arched windows with mullions, a ring of snow-capped gabled dormers around the roof base, a slate-blue spire, and a small lantern with a finial on top, standing in snow. I read this as the Library of Parliament in Ottawa, held loosely.
identifications.cues: Multi-sided drum plan read from the angled faces and buttresses; tall lancet windows; dormered conical roof; crowning lantern and finial; honey sandstone with grey-blue roofing
identifications.moreCertain: The flying buttresses and the corridor linking it to Centre Block. Those are the features that make the Library unmistakable and neither is drawn; without them this is a handsome chapter-house that could be several things

identifications.answer: A modern low-floor articulated city streetcar, drawn larger: red body with a continuous black glazing band, a raked single-ended cab with a large windscreen, headlights and a marker strip at the front, several articulated sections with doors between them, red skirt panels below the windows, standing on a grey rail strip. A present-day tram in the common red-and-black Canadian livery.
identifications.cues: Low floor sitting close to the rail; continuous dark window band; multiple body sections with concertina joints; single cab end with a sloped screen; door pillars breaking the glazing
identifications.moreCertain: A pantograph or trolley pole on the roof, which is absent - nothing here shows how the vehicle draws power, and that plus a route number would confirm both tram and operator

identifications.answer: A combine harvester, drawn larger: red machine body with a glazed cab, an unloading auger arm extended out to the upper left, a large drive wheel and a smaller steering wheel, and at the front right a tan spoked reel above a small white platform, on a stubble field strip. The reel and auger make it a combine rather than a tractor, but the header is barely there - the cutter bar and the full width of the head are not drawn, so the reel reads almost as a loose cogwheel stuck to the front.
identifications.cues: Unloading auger swung out; high glazed cab; big drive wheel; tan spoked reel at the front. Weak: no cutter bar, no header width, no crop being taken in
identifications.moreCertain: A proper header. As drawn the machine's working end is the least legible part of it, which is the wrong way round for a harvester

identifications.answer: A stand of five conifers - spruce or fir - on a grey rocky shelf with pale boulders, shown small. A generic evergreen clump.
identifications.cues: Narrow conical layered silhouettes; two-tone green; thin trunks; grey rock base
