identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for 'conifers' - the shape survives at any size. Species would need cones or bark

identifications.answer: A modern low-floor articulated streetcar drawn large: red body with white waistline stripes, a continuous black glazing band down the side, a rounded single-ended cab with a deep windscreen, two headlights and marker lamps, black door pillars dividing the sections, three dark roof units, and a red skirt below the windows, standing on grooved rail in a paved strip. A present-day city tram.
identifications.cues: Low-floor body hugging the rail; wraparound cab screen; black window band broken by door pillars; grooved street track; red and white livery
identifications.moreCertain: A pantograph. The three dark roof boxes could be air-conditioning or a folded pantograph but nothing reaches up to an overhead wire, so the drawing never shows how it is powered - and a route or operator name would fix the city

identifications.answer: Three small fishing boats lying at moorings: white hulls with blue sheer stripes, low wheelhouses with dark window bands, tall slender masts or outriggers, yellow marker buoys floating beside them, on blue water above a brown quay or shore band. An inshore fishing fleet at anchor.
identifications.cues: Tall thin masts out of proportion to small hulls - the outrigger or stay rig of an inshore boat; white hulls with blue trim; wheelhouse set aft; mooring buoys
identifications.moreCertain: Gear. Nets, traps, drums or booms would say what kind of fishing; as drawn the boats are clean white shapes with masts and nothing aboard them

identifications.answer: A small winter cabin drawn large: horizontal log or board walls in two browns, a wide low-pitched roof with deep eaves carrying snow, two windows with red surrounds glowing warm yellow, a dark plank door in the centre, a bench or log pile under the left window, a small spruce at the right, standing on pale blue ice or packed snow. A warming hut or winter cabin.
identifications.cues: Snow along the roof and eaves; lit yellow windows against dark walls; log courses; spruce beside the door; blue-white ground with faint streak lines
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the ground is a frozen surface or snow-covered land. The streaks in the pale blue read like ice, which would make this a hut on a frozen waterway, but nothing confirms it

identifications.answer: A farmers' market produce stall drawn large: green-and-white striped awning with a scalloped valance over a wooden trestle counter on two posts, three slatted crates holding red apples or tomatoes, tan potatoes or onions, and green cabbages, a wooden barrel with a yellow hoop at the left, a dark crate stored under the table, and two sacks and a broom at the right.
identifications.cues: Scalloped green and white market awning; open trestle counter; produce grouped as coloured spheres in crates; barrel, sacks and broom as market clutter
identifications.moreCertain: A stallholder. The stall is well drawn and clearly a market stall, but it is empty of people, so it reads as furniture rather than as a market in use

identifications.answer: A chateau-style grand hotel drawn large: warm orange-brown brick with tan stone banding, symmetrical wings each ending in a round tower with a tall green copper conical cap and a finial, green copper roofs with dormers between them, a taller central block with a big arched entrance, rows of dark windows, and an arcade of arched openings along the ground floor, with evergreens and snow across the foreground. The Canadian railway chateau hotel type - most likely the Chateau Frontenac, but Chateau Laurier is an equally good fit from this angle.
identifications.cues: Round corner towers with candle-snuffer green roofs; steep dormered copper roofs; warm brick with contrasting stone dressings; arcaded ground floor; grand arched central entrance; symmetrical composition
identifications.moreCertain: The setting again - cliff and river, canal and Parliament, or mountains. The building type is unmistakable; which hotel it is cannot be read from the facade alone

identifications.answer: The rock-shore fishing settlement again, at a very small size: a line of red and white sheds on a boardwalk over water, a spruce treeline behind, and a wide grey bedrock foreground with pools. At this size almost everything except the coloured sheds and the grey rock has gone.
identifications.cues: Coloured shed blocks in a row; sawtooth conifer horizon; dominant grey striated rock
identifications.moreCertain: This is a legibility finding: the boats, the walkway and the water between the stages all disappear, so the strip stops reading as a working harbour and becomes rock with coloured dots

identifications.answer: A chateau-style grand hotel at the largest size in this set, and now dominated by a tall central tower: warm orange brick with tan stone quoins, a massive square central block rising above the wings under a steep dark slate roof with dormers and a needle finial, flanking wings with green copper roofs and round turrets with conical caps, an arcaded ground floor and a deep arched entrance, snow and evergreens in front. The tall central tower pushes me toward the Chateau Frontenac in Quebec City.
identifications.cues: Dominant central tower with a steep dark roof and spike finial - the Frontenac's signature massing; green copper turret caps on the wings; arcaded ground floor; warm brick with stone dressings; symmetrical wings
identifications.moreCertain: The cliff and the river terrace. The tower is the right shape for Frontenac, but it is drawn on a flat snowy base with no Quebec City around it, so the identification rests on massing alone

identifications.answer: A frozen canal skateway in winter at a middling size: a concrete road bridge on piers crossing the back with a balustrade and lamp standards, snowy banks with small spruce, a timber warming hut with a lit window, and six figures skating on the pale blue ice in proper striding poses. Most likely the Rideau Canal Skateway in Ottawa, though nothing here names it.
identifications.cues: Long straight ice between built banks; warming hut on the ice edge; skaters mid-stride with trailing legs; road bridge with lamps; spruce and snow banks
identifications.moreCertain: A landmark that fixes the city. Worth noting the contrast with the other winter-canal art in this set: here the figures are unmistakably skating, there they are seated on sleds

identifications.answer: An ice skater mid-stride: a figure with brown skin and auburn hair in a blue winter coat with white cuffs, a red scarf and a red mitten, grey trousers and brown boots mounted on clearly drawn skate blades, leaning forward with the near leg planted and the far leg trailing behind and one arm swinging across. This is a healthy, readable skating pose - the body weight, the lean and the trailing leg all agree.
identifications.cues: Skate blades drawn under both boots with a cast shadow on the ice; forward body lean over the leading skate; trailing leg extended behind; arm swung across the body for balance; limbs cleanly separated from the torso
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. This is the clearest figure in the hand-off and it reads immediately as skating, which makes the other winter figure in this set - seated on a sled with the torso pitched back - look worse by comparison

identifications.answer: The sternwheel paddle steamer again, smaller: white stacked cabin decks with rows of windows, a big spoked paddlewheel at the stern on the left, a funnel, a pilothouse on top and king posts with spars over the superstructure.
identifications.cues: Stern paddlewheel; three tiers of white cabins; funnel and pilothouse; spar rig above the decks
identifications.moreCertain: The wheel is still legible at this size, which is the feature that matters. A name board would place the boat

identifications.answer: The northern shoreline background strip at its smallest: dark conifer band along the top, a turquoise water band, and a grey stony foreground with green and yellow specks. A generic boreal lake or river shore; at this size it is essentially three coloured bands.
identifications.cues: Three-band composition; conifer sawtooth reduced to texture; turquoise water; grey gravel foreground
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing would identify it. What this size shows is that the shrubs and flowers collapse into noise, leaving stripes

identifications.answer: The chateau-style grand hotel again, small: warm brick wings with green copper roofs and conical turrets, a tall central tower with a steep dark roof and finial, arched ground-floor openings, on a snowy terrace with evergreens below. The railway chateau hotel type - my best guess remains the Chateau Frontenac.
identifications.cues: Central tower over symmetrical wings; green turret caps; brick and stone banding; snow terrace with conifers
identifications.moreCertain: The city around it. The silhouette survives shrinking well, but it identifies a type, not a building

identifications.answer: A frozen canal skateway in winter, drawn large: a concrete road bridge on two heavy piers spanning the back with a railed parapet and three tall lamp standards, a snow-covered bank below, snow-laden spruce, a timber warming hut with a lit window and a door, and five skaters spread across the pale blue ice in proper striding poses, each wearing a toque and coat. Most likely the Rideau Canal Skateway in Ottawa, though nothing here names the city.
identifications.cues: Broad straight ice surface between built banks; warming hut directly on the ice edge; five figures in genuine skating strides with trailing legs; road bridge with lamps overhead; snow banks and frosted spruce
identifications.moreCertain: One identifying landmark. Everything about the scene says maintained public skateway rather than a random frozen river, but the bridge is a plain concrete span that could be anywhere

identifications.answer: Three small fishing boats at moorings, shown small: white hulls with blue trim, low wheelhouses, tall thin masts, yellow buoys, on blue water above a brown quay band.
identifications.cues: Tall thin masts over small white hulls; wheelhouses as dark-windowed blocks; mooring buoys
identifications.moreCertain: Fishing gear of any kind. At this size the boats are white slivers with three vertical lines and could as easily be yachts

identifications.answer: The same pair of grey-beige domes as elsewhere in this set, smaller: a large dome with a dark arched band, a smaller dome to the right, a dark plinth, a blue oval pool in front and a few green shrubs. I still cannot say what it is - a snow house drawn without any white, or a domed building with a reflecting pool.
identifications.cues: Two unequal domes side by side; arched dark band on the large one; blue oval pool; green shrub dots; no colour anywhere else
identifications.moreCertain: Colour, block coursing, or a door. Seeing this object at three sizes now and still not being able to name it is the finding

identifications.answer: The red fishing shack on its wharf at a middling size: deep red boarded walls with white trim, grey-blue gable roof, a window and red double doors, a plank deck on posts with a white railed walkway to the left, stacks of teal crates or traps beneath the deck, a grey boulder at the right, water below.
identifications.cues: Fish-store red with white corner trim; wide double doors; wharf decking on piles; stacked slatted boxes under the deck
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the teal stacks are lobster traps or plain crates - that detail is what would place this on the Atlantic coast rather than any waterfront

identifications.answer: The polygonal Gothic Revival building with the conical roof, shown small: tan sandstone with buttresses, tall arched windows, snow-capped dormers round the roof base, dark spire and finial, standing in snow. I read it as the Library of Parliament, loosely.
identifications.cues: Multi-sided drum with buttresses; lancet windows; dormered conical roof; finial
identifications.moreCertain: Flying buttresses and the link to Centre Block. Without them this stays a generic chapter-house at every size

identifications.answer: A broadleaf tree in autumn colour, small: rounded orange and maroon canopy, short brown trunk, and a few tiny fallen leaves at the base which still show pointed lobes, so still readable as maple.
identifications.cues: Orange and dark red canopy lobes; stubby trunk; small pointed fallen leaves at the foot
identifications.moreCertain: At this size the fallen leaves are a handful of pixels, and they are the only thing saying maple rather than 'orange tree'. Leaf shape in the crown would carry the species down the size ladder

identifications.answer: The white colonial civic building with a clock tower at a middling size: long white block with a dark hipped roof, a columned portico, a blue clock dial with gold hands, an arcaded belfry with gold bells, a green copper dome with a gold ball finial, on a green lawn over a stone base. A town hall, courthouse or colonial legislature; I cannot name it.
identifications.cues: Green dome and gold finial; blue clock face; belfry arches with bells; white classical portico; symmetrical windows
identifications.moreCertain: A setting. This building appears at several sizes in the hand-off and at none of them does anything say which landmark it is meant to be

identifications.answer: The railway lineside strip at small size: two tracks on ballast, telegraph poles with wires, a lineside fence, a red-and-white level-crossing signal beside the line, and green and tan fields behind.
identifications.cues: Track and sleepers running the full width; pole line with sagging wires; small red-and-white crossbuck signal; field bands
identifications.moreCertain: The crossbuck is reduced to a red speck here, so the level-crossing reading nearly goes. A road meeting the track would hold that idea at any size

identifications.answer: A modern city cycling street: a road across the bottom with a blue-painted protected bike lane marked with white bicycle symbols and direction arrows, a green verge above it with street trees, benches, lamp standards and information boards, a bike rack holding two parked bicycles, two helmeted cyclists riding along the verge path, one pedestrian, and a skyline of blue and white glass towers behind a band of water. A contemporary urban cycling corridor - no city is named.
identifications.cues: Blue-surfaced cycle lane with painted bicycle pictograms and arrows; bike rack with parked bikes; helmeted riders; street furniture and trees; generic glass-tower skyline
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the subject - the cycle lane is unmistakable. The skyline is anonymous rectangles again, so the city is not identifiable

identifications.answer: The upright cartoon beaver again with its mouth and front teeth covered by a plain pale rectangle. Tail, belly, ear and body are all present and read as a beaver; the incisors are not visible in this render because a flat box sits over the muzzle.
identifications.cues: Present: cross-hatched paddle tail, cream belly, round ear, stocky upright body. Obscured: muzzle and both incisors, behind a hard-edged light rectangle
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing changes the animal - the tail alone carries it. Recording again that the teeth are not shown here

identifications.answer: The pasture background strip at its smallest: rolling green hills, a fence line, scrub and a dirt track. The cattle that are in the larger versions are no longer visible to me at this size - I can see only faint reddish specks along the fence, which I would not call livestock if I had not seen the bigger render.
identifications.cues: Green hill bands; horizontal fence line; scrub texture; tan track along the bottom
identifications.moreCertain: Size. This is the clearest legibility failure in the set: the subject of the strip - grazing cattle - simply is not there at the size handed over

identifications.answer: A small park bandstand or gazebo pavilion, shown small: octagonal tented roof in green and white radiating stripes with a ball finial, white columns, dark interior with green railing panels, stepped pale base.
identifications.cues: Striped conical roof with finial; ring of white columns; green balustrade; stepped plinth
identifications.moreCertain: Any surrounding context. It reads as a bandstand at every size in this set but never as a particular one

identifications.answer: The pair of grey-beige domes at the largest size, and I still cannot name it. A big dome with a broad dark arched band curving across its face and a dark vertical strip running up behind it, a smaller dome to the right, both on a dark plinth, a blue oval pool with pale streaks in front, and small green shrubs at the base. Read as a snow house it lacks any white or block coursing; read as a domed building it lacks doors, windows and scale.
identifications.cues: Two unequal smooth domes; arched dark band with no depth or opening; blue oval pool; green shrub dots; three near-identical greys carrying the whole form
identifications.moreCertain: Colour and a single piece of surface detail. This asset had four chances at four sizes to tell me what it is and did not, which is the finding rather than a gap in what I was shown

identifications.answer: A small detached house drawn large: cream-yellow clapboard walls with white trim, a blue-grey gable roof, a red brick chimney, an attic window in the gable, two sash windows flanking a pale green front door, a grey picket fence across the front, rounded green shrubs dotted with red berries or flowers, and a green lawn. An ordinary family home.
identifications.cues: Gable front with attic window; chimney; symmetrical windows either side of a central door; picket fence and foundation shrubs
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to read it as a house. If a particular regional house type was intended, none of the markers for one are present

identifications.answer: A stand of five conifers - spruce or fir - drawn large: narrow conical crowns built from layered tiered branch skirts in two greens, slim reddish-brown trunks, standing on a grey rock shelf with two pale rounded boulders.
identifications.cues: Tiered conical silhouettes with stepped branch layers; dark green base tone with a lighter green lit side; thin straight trunks; grey rock base with boulders
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing to call them conifers. Cones, or needle detail, would allow a species; as drawn they are generic spruce-like evergreens, which may well be all that is wanted

identifications.answer: A person riding a skateboard: blond hair, brown skin, a blue winter coat with a red scarf and red mittens, grey trousers with white cuffs and brown boots, standing side-on with both feet on a dark skateboard deck with white wheels, arms held out for balance and knees slightly bent. The pose is sound and readable as skateboarding.
identifications.cues: Skateboard deck with two visible wheel sets under the feet; feet placed across the board, front foot forward; arms out for balance; knees bent; cast shadow beneath the board
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the action. Worth noting the costume: this figure is in the same heavy winter coat, scarf and mittens as the skater, the sledder and the cyclist in this set, which reads oddly on a skateboard

identifications.answer: The coastal waterfront promenade at small size: white picket rail, benches, lamps, green verge and grey walkway, two spruce, deep blue sea carrying a white ferry and a dark red freighter, four standing figures, forested far shore with a grey skyline.
identifications.cues: White ferry and red freighter as coloured slivers on blue; picket rail line; spruce; standing figures
identifications.moreCertain: The ships survive at this size but the people become coloured ticks. Nothing names the port at any size

identifications.answer: Three inshore fishing boats at moorings, drawn large: white hulls with dark blue sheer stripes, low white wheelhouses with dark window bands, tall slender masts each carrying a horizontal spreader, yellow mooring buoys in the water, on a blue harbour above a brown quay band.
identifications.cues: White hulls with blue trim; wheelhouse set forward of an open working deck; tall masts with spreaders; yellow buoys
identifications.moreCertain: Working gear. There are no nets, traps, drums, davits or hauling booms anywhere on these boats, so they read as clean white hulls with masts - closer to pleasure craft than to a fishing fleet

identifications.answer: The railway lineside strip at a middling size: ballasted double track, a red-and-white crossbuck level-crossing signal on a mast, four telegraph poles with sagging wires, a lineside fence, and green and tan fields with hedges behind.
identifications.cues: Crossbuck signal with red lamps; pole line and wires; track and sleepers; boundary fence; field bands
identifications.moreCertain: A road crossing the track. The signal is the only thing saying 'crossing' and there is no roadway to cross

identifications.answer: The city cycling street at small size: blue-painted bike lane with white bicycle symbols along the bottom, green verge with trees, benches, lamps and sign boards, a bike rack with parked bikes, two cyclists and a pedestrian, and a glass-tower skyline behind.
identifications.cues: Blue lane with repeated bicycle pictograms - still the clearest cue at this size; tree and lamp rhythm; small rider figures
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the subject. The painted lane markings survive the reduction well, which is the right thing to have survive

identifications.answer: A snow-capped masonry wall corner, small: coursed tan stone blocks returning around a corner, a brown coping band, snow along the top and a drift at the foot. A fragment of stonework with nothing to identify it.
identifications.cues: Ashlar courses on two faces; corner return; snow cap and drift; no opening or feature
identifications.moreCertain: Anything beyond the wall itself. At this size it is a beige box with a white line on top

identifications.answer: The red barn with its paddock at small size: red gabled barn with a roof cupola and a lean-to stable wing, a post-and-rail paddock on sandy ground. There is a pale shape inside the paddock which I know from the larger renders is meant to be a horse, but at this size it is an indistinct white blob and I would not identify it as an animal on its own.
identifications.cues: Barn: red mass, grey roof, cupola, lean-to wing. Paddock: fence line. Horse: unresolved pale patch
identifications.moreCertain: The horse needs redrawing. The barn survives the size ladder; the animal in front of it does not read as a horse at any size in this set

identifications.answer: A park bandstand or gazebo pavilion at a middling size: octagonal tented roof in radiating green and white stripes with a scalloped valance and a ball finial, a ring of white columns, dark shaded interior with green railing panels between the columns, stepped pale stone base.
identifications.cues: Striped conical roof with scalloped edge and finial; white column ring; green balustrade panels; stepped plinth
identifications.moreCertain: Context. It is clearly a bandstand and never more than that - no park, no waterfront, no sign

identifications.answer: Toronto City Hall - Viljo Revell's New City Hall on Nathan Phillips Square - drawn large. Two curved concave towers of unequal height standing back to back with their banded window strips facing inward, the low domed clamshell council chamber sitting between them on the podium, a long colonnaded podium below and a blue reflecting pool across the front. Confident.
identifications.cues: The paired curved slabs of different heights facing each other; the saucer council chamber nested between them on its stalk; horizontal window banding on the concave faces; pale concrete end walls; podium colonnade with the rectangular pool
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. The silhouette is unique and is drawn accurately, including the ribbed curve of the tower faces

identifications.answer: A harbourfront boardwalk in a small coastal town: a timber boardwalk with mooring bollards, globe lamp standards and benches, a brown timber kiosk or shop with a notice board, small boats moored in the water just behind, gulls perched and flying, people standing and sitting along the walk, and a townscape of white and tan hipped-roof houses with a church spire and a few taller blocks behind. A working waterfront promenade - no place name.
identifications.cues: Boardwalk decking with bollards and cleats; moored boats immediately behind the walk; gulls; kiosk with a posted notice; dense low townscape with a steeple
identifications.moreCertain: A named building or a harbour shape. The boardwalk and boats say working seaport but the town behind is generic

identifications.answer: The upright cartoon beaver with its paddle tail absent and a hard rectangular notch cut out of the body at the left hip and forearm, leaving a straight vertical edge in the fur. Teeth, ear, muzzle and belly are present. Same missing-tail state as another render in this set.
identifications.cues: Present: buck incisors, cream muzzle and belly, round ear, upright body. Absent: the paddle tail entirely, and a squared bite out of the silhouette between hip and forearm
identifications.moreCertain: Whether the tail was painted out for this hand-off or is genuinely missing from the asset. I cannot tell from inside, and I will not report a tail that is not on screen

identifications.answer: Four hopper-bottom grain storage bins on a concrete pad, small: tan-grey cylinders with ring seams and peaked conical roofs with cap vents, a ladder on one, cone bottoms on steel legs. Farm grain bins.
identifications.cues: Conical roofs with caps; hopper cones on legs; ring seams; poured pad
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. Same note as at full size: these are bins, not a wooden grain elevator, and they are drawn in a notably flat, desaturated grey-tan

identifications.answer: The city waterfront park strip at a small-to-middling size: terraced paved walkway with lamps, benches and a few small figures, three round-crowned trees - two autumn orange, one green - a pale water band, and a grey and blue tower skyline behind.
identifications.cues: Three lollipop trees; banded paving; lamp and bench rhythm; flat rectangular skyline
identifications.moreCertain: An identifiable building in the skyline, which this asset never has at any size

identifications.answer: A combine harvester at the largest size: red-orange body with a dark grain tank, a white-roofed glazed cab, an unloading auger folded up and out to the left, one large drive wheel and one smaller wheel, and at the front right a small orange box carrying a tan spoked reel above a white platform. The machine reads as a combine, but the header is the weakest part of the drawing - there is no cutter bar and no header width, so the reel sits on a little box like a cogwheel bolted to the front.
identifications.cues: Folded unloading auger; glazed cab above a grain tank; large drive wheel; tan spoked reel. Missing: cutter bar, full-width header, crop
identifications.moreCertain: A properly drawn header. At full size the omission is more obvious, not less - the business end of the machine is a stub

identifications.answer: The heritage streetcar street scene at small size: a green-and-cream tram on rails at the left, a pale building with twin chimneys and a red-and-white awning behind, a red-brick commercial block with an arched entrance in the middle, a white building at the right, rails along the street.
identifications.cues: Green tram body with a window band; brick block with cornice; paired chimneys; street rails
identifications.moreCertain: Lettering on the tram, or a civic landmark. The scene survives shrinking but was never place-specific

identifications.answer: A railway car carrying two stacked intermodal containers at small size: grey car on two trucks, a blue container on the deck and a rust-red one on top, on sleepered track.
identifications.cues: Two ribbed container boxes stacked; grey car body; trucks; track
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing for the type - a double-stack car reads at this size. The overhang of both containers past the car ends is still visible and still looks wrong

identifications.answer: The frozen canal scene with sledders at a small-to-middling size: stone embankment with a dark green iron railing, cluster globe lamps, benches with seated figures, a small shelter, a heavy timber trestle frame at the left, and three figures out on the pale ice seated on sleds.
identifications.cues: Walled straight ice channel; green railing and globe lamps; shelter and benches; three seated figures on the ice
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing names the city. And the figures on the ice are sledders, where the other winter-canal art in this set shows skaters - the two scenes do not say the same thing about what the place is for

identifications.answer: Still not confidently identifiable, but at this largest size I can revise my reading. Several long tapering cylinders lie crossed over one another, each with a dark circular cap at its end that reads as cut end-grain, over a pale flat slab, with a cluster of four or five short stubby prongs rising near the middle-left and pale oval shapes scattered on the dark ground strip. My best reading is now a stack of cut logs or timber, with the prongs as broken branch stubs. Against that: there is no wood colour anywhere - the whole thing is three flat greys and a beige - and no bark, grain or ring detail.
identifications.cues: Long cylinders with dark circular end caps, reading as sawn log ends; crossed stacking; short branch-stub cluster; pale ovals on the ground; complete absence of brown or any saturated colour
identifications.moreCertain: Colour above all - brown bark and paler cut ends would make this obvious instantly. This asset appears four times in the hand-off and is the least legible thing in it at every size

identifications.answer: A snow-capped masonry wall corner drawn large: tan and beige dressed stone blocks laid in courses with darker brown bands, returning around a corner so both faces show, a snow cap along the top coping and a curved snow drift at the foot. A fragment of stonework - nothing identifies what it belongs to.
identifications.cues: Coursed ashlar with drawn joints on both faces; corner return giving depth; brown banding courses; snow cap and drift
identifications.moreCertain: The rest of the structure. Even at full size this is a wall corner and no more - it could be a lock, a rampart, a bridge abutment or a retaining wall

identifications.answer: The small detached house at a middling size: cream-yellow walls, blue-grey gable roof, brick chimney, attic window, two sash windows either side of a pale green door, grey picket fence, green shrubs with red berries, lawn.
identifications.cues: Gable with attic window and chimney; symmetrical windows; picket fence; berry shrubs
identifications.moreCertain: Nothing. An ordinary house at every size; no regional house type is legible

identifications.answer: Two cartoon characters facing each other: on the left a woman with long auburn hair and pale skin in a blue winter parka with a red scarf, red mitten, grey trousers with white cuffs and brown boots; on the right an RCMP officer in Red Serge - tan Stetson, scarlet tunic, Sam Browne cross strap, blue breeches with yellow stripe, brown riding boots. Same two roles as elsewhere in this set with different casting.
identifications.cues: Mountie uniform complete; civilian in parka, scarf and mitten; identical cartoon proportions and outlines on both
